translations.text: [?] Alpha [?] Omega [?] Jesus [?] Christ [?]. A eulogy delivered by our holy father, honored in every way, Apa Timothy, the archbishop of Alexandria. He delivered it concerning the appointment of Abbaton, the angel of death.
When our holy fathers, the apostles, asked the Savior about him so that they could proclaim him to all humanity, knowing that people would inquire of them about everything,

the Savior did not wish to disappoint them in anything they asked of him. He told them, “The day on which my Father appointed him was the thirteenth of the month of Hathor. He made him king over the whole creation that he had made, because of the transgression of Adam and Eve.”

The archbishop himself also wished to understand how God had made him an object of fear and terror, coming for every soul until they surrender their spirit in misery. When he went to Jerusalem to worship at the cross of our Savior and his life-giving tomb, on the seventeenth of the month of Thout, he searched the books in the library of Jerusalem, which our holy fathers, the apostles, had compiled and left there, until he learned about his appointment through an elderly priest from Jerusalem.
When he asked him about the reason for this matter, since the matter concerned him.

He also spoke about the theologian and virgin, the holy apostle Saint John, saying that he would not taste death until the thrones were prepared in the valley of Jehoshaphat, which is the place where the final struggle of the world will take place.
In the peace of God. Amen. Bless us.
I hear the one whose mouth is sweet and full of every joy,
my Lord and my God, calling out to us daily in the holy Gospels: “Everyone who asks will receive, and whoever seeks will find, and whoever knocks will have the door opened for him.”
And again: “Whatever you ask of my Father in my name will be yours.”
The holy songwriter David also says, “Blessed are those who are holy along the way, and those who walk in the law of the Lord.”
Blessed are the holy ones and those who seek them.
Blessed are those who examine his testimonies, those who seek him with their whole heart.
And again: “Those who seek the Lord will not lack any good thing.”
Who are those who seek the Lord?
My beloved, listen attentively, you who love to listen.
Those who seek the Lord are all who meditate on his law, his commandments, and his ordinances day and night, as it is written: “The law of God must not depart from your mouth.”
And again: “Every Christian should satisfy himself with the fruits of his lips as with bodily food.”
Those who seek the Lord are all who inquire into the appointment of God's angels and make their holy commemoration known.
Those who seek the Lord are all who seek his saints, who care about the sufferings they endured and place them in the churches.
Those who seek the Lord are all who give charitable gifts and offerings to God at their holy commemoration, each according to his ability.
Those who seek the Lord are all who welcome strangers and love the poor, clothing those who are naked at the feast of the saints, each according to his ability.
Therefore, my beloved brothers, let us give on the day of the saints, each according to his ability.
Therefore, my beloved brothers, let us give with an upright heart and complete faith, so that we may find them beside us on the day of our visitation.
Our Savior tells us in the holy Gospel, “Whoever gives one of these little ones even a cup of cold water to drink in the name of a disciple—truly, I say [?]” [Three leaves missing.]
A week before the festival came.
And so we went to the shrine of the holy Mother of God, Mary, which had been built for her in the valley of Jehoshaphat. We received her blessing and prayed with those who had come to the festival.
And so he attended to the offering. We assembled with all the people that day.
Each person went home, while we awaited the festival. But I stayed in the church.

While we were still sitting there, an elderly priest named John approached me and asked me, saying, “If your servant has found favor in your sight, let my lord and father come to your servant’s house, so that we may enjoy your blessing.”
When I saw his great love for humanity and his cheerfulness, like an angel of God, I got up and went with him, along with those who were with me.
After he had taken us upstairs to a room in his house, we prayed and sat down according to the commandment of our Savior.
And he prepared a great feast for us that day, because he was a generous man, especially toward strangers and everyone who came to the church, like the patriarch Abraham.
When morning came, we spoke with one another about the mighty deeds and wonders our Savior had performed, and how the godless Jews had killed him because of their envy of him.
And so I said to the elderly priest, “My honored son, among all these books, has the book about the appointment of Abbaton, the angel of death, come into your possession?

For I long for it, so that I may learn how God made him king over all humanity and all the creation he had made, and how God made him a source of fear and trembling, coming and going after every soul until they give up their spirit.”

Immediately the elderly priest said to me, with a face full of grace, “Christ, the teacher of us all, spoke well in the holy Gospel when he said, ‘The one who seeks will find; for the one who knocks, the door will be opened; and the one who asks will receive.’
But you, my holy father, have sought and found; you have knocked, and the door has been opened for you; you have asked and received.
The Lord will fulfill the request you have made.”
When I heard these things from the elderly priest, I thanked God, because he had not disappointed me in anything I sought from him. And so he brought it to me.
When it came into my hands, I rejoiced over it more than over an immense fortune.
I too cried out with David, the psalmist and righteous king, “I will rejoice over your word like someone who has found abundant plunder.”
Then I read in it.
I found it written as follows:

“It happened that when our Savior, the very root of all goodness, had completed everything, and the days of his ascension had been fulfilled, so that he might go up to his Father, he laid his hand on each of his holy apostles.
He prayed over them, so that he might send them out into the whole world to proclaim his holy resurrection to all the nations.
He filled them with power and the Holy Spirit, saying to them, ‘The mighty deeds and wonders that I have performed, you too will perform.
You will lay your hands on the sick, and they will recover.
You will tread on snakes and scorpions.
You will pick up snakes in your hands.
If you drink a deadly poison, it will not harm you.’
Those who believe in me, my good Father, and the Holy Spirit—baptize them in the name of the Father, the Son, and the Holy Spirit. I too will forgive them.
Those who do not believe will be condemned to the second death.
Go in peace.
May my own peace be with you.
But I will not stop walking with you until the end of this age.

Then Saint Peter, the great apostle, the pillar of the church and the steward of the kingdom of heaven, answered him, saying, “Whoever you want to bring into it, bring in; and whoever you want to throw out, throw out.”
He also said to the Savior, “My Lord and my God, you have told us everything we asked of you. You have hidden nothing from us.

Now, therefore, my Lord and my God, you are sending us out into the whole world to proclaim your holy resurrection to all the nations, the mighty deeds and wonders you performed, which we saw with our own eyes, and the things we hear about. You have revealed them all to us, even your virgin mother and your holy birth.
And you know, my Lord, that there are many quarrelsome people and unbelievers in the world. They will question us about everything. We want to be able to give them an answer about every matter.

Now, therefore, my Lord, we want you to tell us about the day when you appointed Abbaton as the angel of death, and how you made him a terror and a source of trembling, coming after every soul until people give up their spirits. Then we can proclaim him to all humanity, just like all his fellow angels whom you created, whose day of appointment you have told us about. And when people hear about the day of his appointment, they may be afraid and repent and give charitable offerings and alms on the day of his commemoration, as they do for Michael and Gabriel, so that their souls may find mercy and rest on the day of your holy resurrection.”

But the merciful Savior, who is full of mercy and every kind of compassion, who desires what is good for his creation, did not want to cause us sorrow concerning anything that might be asked of us. He said to them, “You whom I have chosen from the whole world, I will hide nothing from you. Instead, I will tell you how my Father appointed him over the whole creation that he made.
For my Father and I are one. As Philip said to me, ‘Lord, show us your Father, and that will be enough for us.’
I said to him, ‘You have been with me all this time, and you have not known me, Philip?
Whoever has seen me has seen my Father.
Believe that I am in my Father and my Father is in me.
Otherwise, believe his works.’
Now, therefore, my holy members, whom I have chosen from the whole world, I will hide nothing from you.

When my Father created heaven and earth and everything in them, he spoke, and they all came into being: angels, archangels, cherubim, seraphim, thrones, dominions, principalities, authorities, and all the powers of heaven,
and the whole host of heaven. On earth he also created the wild animals, reptiles, livestock, birds, and everything that moves upon it.
He also planted a paradise in the east.
My Father saw that the whole world was deserted, with no one to work it.

My Father said, ‘Let us make a human being according to our likeness and our image, so that he may continually bless us day and night, and they may know that it is the hand of the Lord that created all these things, for I exist before these things came into being.’

My Father commanded an angel, saying, “Go, according to my will and my command, to the land of Eden, and bring me virgin soil, so that I may make a human being according to our likeness and our image, and he may continue to bless us day and night.”
The angel went to the land of Eden according to my Father’s command. He stood over the clay and stretched out his hand to take it to my Father.

Immediately the clay cried out in a loud voice, saying, “I adjure you by the one who sent you to me! If you take me to him and he shapes me into a human being with a living soul, great sins will come from me. Much sexual immorality, slander, envy, hatred, and strife will arise through him.
Many murderers and people who shed blood will arise through him.
They will throw me to their dogs and pigs, and into wells and pits and [?], before my time. After all these things, they will throw me into punishments and torment me day and night.
Leave me alone, sleeping and at rest.”
When the angel of the Lord heard these things, he became afraid because of my Father’s name.
He turned back and came to my Father. He said, “My Lord, when I heard your fearsome name, I could not bring it to you.”
Immediately he commanded the second angel and sent him to it, and likewise the third, down to the seventh angel. They could not approach it, because it adjured them with great and fearsome oaths.

When my Father saw that they could not bring it to him, he sent the angel Muriel to it, saying to him, “Go at my command to the land of Eden and bring me virgin clay, so that I may shape it into a human being according to my likeness and my image, and he may bless us day and night.”
When the angel of the Lord went to it, he stood over it with great power and firmness and with the Lord’s command.
He stretched out his hand to take it.
Immediately the clay cried out in a loud voice, “I adjure you by the one who established heaven and earth and everything in them! If you approach me to take me to God—”
But the angel Muriel was not afraid because of my Father’s name when he heard it, nor did he have pity on it. Instead, he rushed at it and seized it with force and determination.
He brought it to my Father, who rejoiced over it.
He took the clay from the angel’s hand and made Adam according to our likeness and our image. He left him lying there for forty days and forty nights without giving him spirit.
He sighed over him every day, saying, “There are great sufferings [?] this one if I give him spirit.”
I said to my Father, “Give him spirit, and I will be his guarantor.”

My Father said to me, “If I give him spirit, my beloved Son, you will have to go down into the world and endure great sufferings because of him, until you save him and restore him to his original state.”
I said to my Father, “Give him spirit. I will be his guarantor, and I will go down into the world and fulfill your command.”

When he was about to give him spirit, he took the book and recorded those who would come from him and enter the kingdom of heaven, as it is written: “Those whose names are written in the book of life from the foundation of the world.”
And in this way he gave him the spirit of life. He breathed the breath of life into his face three times, saying, “Live! Live! Live! According to the pattern of my divinity.”
And immediately he came to life and became a living soul, according to the likeness and image of God.
When Adam stood up, he bowed down before the Father, saying, “My Lord and my God,
you brought me into being when I did not exist.”

And in this way my Father seated him on a great throne and placed on him a crown of glory and a royal scepter. My Father commanded every order in heaven to come and worship him, whether angels or archangels.
The entire heavenly army came and bowed down first to God. Afterward they bowed down to Adam, saying, “Greetings, likeness and image of God!”
The order to bow down to the first-formed man also reached him. My Father said to him, “You too, come and bow down to my likeness and my image.”
But great pride and shamelessness rose up in him. He said, “This one should come and bow down to me instead, because I existed before he came into being.”

When my Father saw his great arrogance, and that his wickedness and evil deeds had reached their full measure, he commanded all the orders of heaven, saying to them, “Come, take the document from the arrogant one's hand, strip him of his armor, and throw him down onto the earth, for his time has come.”
For he was greater than all of them and was their head, just as a king gives an army of soldiers to a general to be their head, with their names registered with him.
This was how it was with this master of deceit: the angels were registered with him.
All the angels gathered around him, but they could not take the document from him.
My Father commanded them to bring a sharp knife and cut it on this side and that. They could not take from him the part that was inside, under the palm of his hand.

Immediately my Father gave an order to a great cherub, who struck him and threw him down from heaven onto the earth because of his arrogance. He broke his wing and his side and made him weak. Those whom he had brought out with him became devils along with him.
But my Father had Adam taken into paradise, with a multitude of angels singing psalms before him. They left him there, and he remained, praising God.

Adam was alone in paradise for a hundred years. When he had completed the hundred years, while Adam was living in the paradise of delight, alone and in need, and the angels were coming to him daily, my Father said, “It is not good for the man to remain alone. Instead, let us make him a helper suited to him.”
He brought a deep sleep upon Adam, and Adam fell asleep. He took one of his ribs, filled it with flesh, and made a woman in Adam's likeness.
When Adam awoke from the deep sleep, he saw her and said, “This now is a bone from my bones, and this is flesh. She will be called woman, because she was taken from her man.”

For Adam was the one who named all the livestock, the wild animals, the birds, and every living creature that moves on the earth, even those in the waters of the rivers. Adam named them all according to the command of my good Father.
Adam lived in the paradise of delight with Eve his wife for two hundred years. They were virgins, living like the angels of God.

After they had completed two hundred years living in the paradise of delight, Eve came walking along the north side of paradise, beside the fence, to get fruit for the livestock and all the other living creatures. For my Father had told them to give the creatures food according to his command, and they received their food from Adam and Eve.
The serpent, too, came at evening to receive its food as usual. For the serpent was like all the wild animals, walking on its feet as they did.

The devil was beside paradise, plotting against them day and night. When he saw her alone, he entered the serpent and said to himself within it, “Look, I have found my opportunity against them. I will speak into her ears and see whether I can make her eat from the tree, so that they will be thrown out of paradise, just as I myself was thrown out.”
He said to her through the serpent’s mouth, “Why do you not eat from the tree in the middle of paradise as you do from all the other trees? Its fruit is beautiful.”
But he said, “The Lord told us to eat freely from every tree in paradise except this tree of the knowledge of good and evil. On the day you eat from it, you will surely die.”
But the serpent said to her, “You will not die. Instead, you will become like the gods, knowing good and evil and distinguishing what is sweet from what is bitter.
That is why God told you this: so that you would not eat and become like the gods.”
And he did not stop speaking to her until he led her astray and she ate from the tree.
Immediately she became naked and realized that she was naked. She took fig leaves and covered her nakedness.
Then Eve went to Adam. When Adam saw her naked, he was deeply saddened. He was filled with great anguish and many tears.
He said to her, “Why have you become like this?
Look, from today onward we will die, and the Lord will be angry with us and throw us out of paradise.”
But she said to him, “Come and eat. If God threatens you, I will take all the blame upon myself before God.”
And so Adam took it and ate. He became naked and immediately realized that he was naked. He covered his nakedness with fig leaves.
Immediately my Father’s voice came to him in paradise: “Adam, where are you?”
He said, “My Lord, I heard your voice, and I was afraid and hid myself because I am naked.”
My Father said to him, “Who told you to eat from the tree so that you became naked?”
He said, “My Lord, the woman you gave me as a helper led me astray, and I became naked.”
My Father said to her, “Why did you do this?”
She said, “My Lord, Lord, the serpent deceived me. I ate so that I might become like the gods.”
My Father said to the serpent, “Because you have done this, you are cursed among all the wild animals of the earth.
You will crawl on your belly all the days of your life, you and all your offspring, throughout all the generations of the earth.
You will eat dust and ashes all your days, you and all who descend from you.”
And so he began crawling on his belly, just as my Father had decreed concerning him.
He also said to the woman, “Because you have done this, you will give birth to your children in pain and groaning, and you will turn toward deliverance.”
Then he turned to Adam and said to him, “The ground is cursed because of your deeds. You will eat your bread by the sweat of your face, you and all who descend from you.
Look, from today onward you will die, because you are dust, and you will return to the dust again.
You will live in this world for nine hundred and thirty years. Then death will come upon you, and you will return to the dust once more.”
Your soul too will be in Hades, while you sit in the sealed darkness for four and a half thousand years.
In the five-and-a-half-thousandth year, I will send my beloved Son into the world. He will remain in a virgin's womb for nine months—that is, Mary, the holy virgin.
She will give birth to him on earth as a poor man, and she will remain a virgin, just as she was.
He will spend thirty-three and a half years in the world. He will experience everything belonging to human life, except sin alone.

He will perform a multitude of mighty deeds and wonders beyond counting. He will raise the dead and cast out demons. He will heal the paralyzed and make the lame walk again. He will make the mute hear; he will make them speak. He will cleanse those with leprosy and the withered hands. He will open the eyes of the blind through the word of his power.
In short, the wonders he will perform will be beyond counting, and despite all these things, they will not believe in him.
But at the end of all these things, they will rise up against him and hand him over to death. They will deliver him into the hands of a governor named Pilate, who will judge him for your sake.
He will take the form of a slave for your sake.
They will spit in his face for your sake.
They will insult him and humiliate him for your sake.
They will pass judgment on him as they do on criminals.
They will raise him onto the wood of a cross between two robbers for your sake.
They will put a crown of thorns on his head.
They will give him vinegar and gall to drink because of you.
They will put nails into his hands and feet because of you.
He will give up his spirit on the cross, and they will pierce his side with a spear. Water and blood will come out of it, and these will cleanse the sins of the world.

They will place him in a new tomb, and he will rise from the dead on the third day. He will descend into the underworld, shatter the bronze gates, break the iron bars, and bring you up along with all the captives who are with you.

Because of you, Adam, the Son of God will endure all these things until he saves you and returns you once again to paradise, to the place from which you originally came. For he took pains over you while you were clay, before he breathed spirit into you.
I am the Son of God. I endured all these things until I saved humanity from the devil’s power.
And you saw all these things with your own eyes, my holy apostles.
And in this way my Father cast Adam and Eve out of paradise.
He shut the gate and stationed a fiery power to guard the gate of paradise, so that no one would enter it until everything he had said concerning Adam was fulfilled.

The devil met Adam outside paradise. He said to him, “Look, Adam! I was cast out of my glory because of you. Look! I too have caused you to be cast out of the paradise of delight, because you made me an exile from my dwelling place in heaven.
Know this: I will not stop fighting against you and those who come after you—all those who descend from you—until I bring them all down to Hades with me.”
When Adam heard these things, he was filled with anguish and wept bitterly day and night.
My Father said to the angel Muriel, “Look! Here is the man whom I created in my likeness. He has transgressed the commandment that I gave him.
He ate from the tree and brought great harm upon all humanity.
For this reason I will make you king over him, because you are the one who brought him to me on this day, which is the thirteenth of Hathor.
Your name will be fearful in everyone's mouth. They will call you Abaddon, the angel of death.
Your appearance and your form will bring growling, anger, and menace against every soul until they give up their spirit.
Your eyes and your face will be like the wheels of fire rising in wave after wave before me.
The sound of your nostrils will be like the sound of the lake of fire burning with fire and smoke.
The rumbling sound from your lips will be like the sound of the seven trumpets when they speak with their tongues.
Your head will be like these great pillars of fire, stretching from heaven down below.
Your teeth will project outside your mouth for half a cubit in length.
The fingers of your hands and the toes of your feet will be like sharp sickles.
Seven heads will be on top of your head, differing in their appearance and form.
Their teeth will project outside their mouths for two handbreadths in length, and they will look toward the four sides of the world.
You will be suspended in the middle, sitting on a throne of fire.

Your eyes will see everything beneath the earth, even what is in the waters of the rivers. Nothing beneath heaven will be hidden from you, from one end of the earth to the other, from north to south and from east to west, throughout the whole creation that I have made.
Not a single person will give up their spirit until they have all seen you.
You will have no pity on either the small or the great. You will take them all without sparing anyone.
Powers will stand before you, and you will send them after every soul.
They will keep terrifying them, changing their forms.

When the hour of their lifetime is complete, you will reveal yourself, and they will see you. When they see your face, their souls will not remain within them for a single hour without their giving up their spirit.
You will remain like this, reigning over them until the appointed time that I have given the world is complete.
When the angels saw him, they were thrown into confusion among themselves, saying, “Woe! Woe to the human beings who will be born into the world!
Look, we are bodiless beings, yet we have come undone with fear.”
Then Abbaton, the angel of death, bowed down before my Father, saying, “My Lord, look, you have made me more terrifying than all the angels.

Now, therefore, my Lord, I implore you and appeal to your goodness: if the human beings who will be born into the world hear how you have made me a source of fear and terror, and they become afraid and give charitable gifts and alms in my name, and copy the book of the day on which you appointed me, commemorating me and seeking mercy and rest for their souls—

now, therefore, my Lord, let your mercy reach them. Give me authority over them so that I may take them to the places of rest, the dwelling place of all who rejoice, because they have commemorated me on earth, just as they commemorate all my fellow angels.
Yes, my Lord, let your mercy reach them.”

My Father said, “I tell you, Abbaton the angel: anyone who fears you and gives charitable gifts and alms in your name, repents, and copies the book of your appointment—which is on the thirteenth day of the month of Hathor, the day on which I appointed you over Adam because of his disobedience—I will write their names in the book of life and grant them to you in my kingdom. They will not experience any torment.
You will not go to them in these terrifying forms. Instead, you will go to them cheerfully, until you bring them out of the body.
I will give you authority over them, and you will take them to the places of rest, the dwelling place of all who rejoice, because I am a good God, compassionate toward what I have created.”
Then Abbaton the angel bowed down before my Father, saying, “What shall I give you in return, Lord, my God and my king, for everything you have done for me?”

Now, therefore, my holy apostles, look, I have told you how my Father made Abbaton a source of fear and terror over the whole creation that he made, because of the transgression of Adam and Eve. Proclaim this to all humanity.

Saint John the virgin replied, saying, “My Lord and my God, who purified me for himself and kept all my thoughts fixed on him, who kept me from taking a wife: on the day of your resurrection, when you gather all your creation into the valley of Jehoshaphat so that everyone receives according to what they have done, whether good or evil, will Abbaton, the angel of death, come again on that day in forms like these? If so, my Lord, not a single soul will be able to stand before your terrifying judgment seat.
Look, we have melted with fear as we hear these things from you.”

The Son smiled at John and said to him, “O John, my beloved, the one who leaned upon my breast because of the purity of his heart, the purity of his holy body, and his virginity! Do you not know that on the day of my holy resurrection they neither take wives nor live with husbands? Nor will there be death, because the old things have passed away, except for the second death for those who will come to it.
On the day of my holy resurrection, I will come on the clouds of heaven, and every eye will see me, and all the tribes and languages will mourn,
with thousands upon thousands and tens of thousands upon tens of thousands of angels before me.
My cross will advance before me like the standards before their king, just as I told you: ‘The Son of Man will come in his glory and that of his Father, with all his angels accompanying him.’

I will command my great holy archangel Michael to sound the trumpet in the valley of Jehoshaphat, and the dead will rise incorruptible. Not a single soul will be able to remain upon the earth without rising, from Adam, the first human being, down to the last human being who will be born into the world.
They will all come to the valley of Jehoshaphat, and everyone will receive according to what they have done through their body, whether good or evil.
They will stand in fear and trembling, awaiting the mercy of my Father.

But you, O my beloved John, will not die until the thrones are prepared on the day of the holy resurrection. For glorious thrones will descend from heaven, and you will sit upon them, while I sit in your midst.
All the saints will see the honor that I will give you, O my beloved John.
I will command the angel Abbaton to come to you on that day without any terrifying appearance. Instead, he will come to you with a cheerful face, like Michael, and take your soul and bring it to me.
Your body will never be in a tomb, nor will earth ever lie upon it.
All the saints will marvel at you, because they will not be able to pass judgment until you pass judgment with them.
You will spend three quarters of an hour dead, lying upon your throne, while all creation watches you.
I will return your soul to your body once more, and you will rise clothed in a robe of glory, like someone who has risen from a bridal chamber.
You will judge the whole world, just as I established with you, saying, ‘You will sit upon the thrones and judge the twelve tribes of Israel.’
And I said through the mouth of Paul, ‘We will judge angels, even before we come to the affairs of the world.’

For on that day all creation will stand in fear and trembling. I will give the order, and they will be separated from one another as a shepherd separates the sheep from the goats: the righteous on the right and the sinners on the left. No one will be able to utter a sound until the Ancient of Days gives them permission.
I will look upon all my creation and see that it is going to destruction. I will cry out to my Father, ‘My Father, what good is my blood if what I created is going to destruction?’

At once my Father’s voice will come to me from the seventh heaven, with no one hearing it except me alone, because my Father and I are one: “The authority is yours, my Son, to do whatever pleases you with what you have created.”
And on that day I too will say joyfully, “You have removed my sackcloth and clothed me in gladness, so that my right hand will bless you without sorrow.”

On that day I will say to you, my holy apostles, and to all my holy ones—whether angels or archangels, prophets or righteous people—and especially to my virgin mother and my great archangel Michael and Gabriel: “Do not let anyone go to destruction who has commemorated you on earth and given bread in your name.”
And at once all the saints will approach them. Each one will take those who belong to him, everyone
who has done what is true on earth, and they will bring them all over beside the others who are on the right.
Then the others will cry out with loud weeping, distressed at heart, saying, “Lord, merciful one, Son of the merciful one, have mercy on us too!”
At that moment the Son of God will weep over them and say to them, “Wait while I speak with my Father.”
At once my Father will shut the gates of heaven and withdraw.
I will then say to them, “My Father was unwilling to have mercy on you.”
And they will cry out even more, “Have mercy on us, because the devil did not let us repent.
If we had known that these things would happen, we would have repented to the point of pouring out—pouring out blood.”

And at once, on that day, I will curse Satan and have him seized and bound with chains that cannot be undone, together with the false prophet who deceives all the nations and the Antichrist, the son of destruction. They will be thrown into the lake of fire that burns with fire and sulfur, along with all those in the world who followed him. They will have no rest day or night,
nor will their worm die, and their fire will not be extinguished.
Now then, holy apostles, look: I have told you everything you asked me about, including how Adam transgressed until death entered the world, and how the angel Abaddon became king over all creation.
Now proclaim the day of his commemoration, so that human beings will be afraid and repent.
Tell all humanity, saying, “Whoever does good will rise to life.
Whoever does evil will rise to judgment.”
Then the apostles worshiped the Savior, saying, “Our Lord and our God, you have filled us with every blessing, because you have not disappointed us in anything we asked of you.”
The Savior greeted them, and the angels carried him up to heaven while they watched him.
The apostles, for their part, worshiped him, and each one went out to preach, just as he had commanded them.

These things, my beloved, we have told you according to what we found in the library of Jerusalem, which our holy fathers, the apostles, compiled and deposited there for the faithful and for the salvation of unbelievers.
Now then, my beloved, let us be eager to give charitable gifts and alms on the day commemorating Abbaton, the angel of death, each according to their ability.

Remember what is written in the Gospel: our Savior praised the poor woman who put in the two small coins above all those who put money into the treasury. “All these,” he said, “gave out of their surplus, but she, in her poverty, gave everything she had.”
May God, who made us worthy to gather in this place today to commemorate Abaddon, the angel of death, whom God made king over us, make us worthy to be gathered into his kingdom in heaven.
All of us, my beloved, need God’s mercy, as a wise man said: “Just as I want to live, I want everyone to live.”

May it be so, my beloved friends: may he make us worthy to hear the blessed voice, full of every joy: “Come, you who are blessed by my Father, inherit the kingdom prepared for you since the foundation of the world.” Through the grace and love for humanity of our Lord Jesus Christ, through whom glory belongs to him, his good Father, and the Holy Spirit forever and ever. Amen.
Remember me with love, everyone who reads this book, so that God may forgive me my many sins—I, Theopistus, the least of all.
Written in the month of Thoth, on the eleventh, indiction [?], in the year 698 of the holy martyrs. [?]

Through the zeal and care of our distinguished, God-loving brother Michael, the son of the blessed Stephen, the farmer from Moui. He took care of this little book through his own labor and donated it to the monastery of Saint Mercurius in the city of Tbo for the salvation of his soul, so that it might be read in honor of Abbaton, the angel of death, and so that Saint Mercurius might intercede with Christ for him, that he might bless him in this world, save him from all the snares of the devil and wicked people, and help him in every good work. And when he departs from this life, may the archangel Abbaton reconcile him to God, and may God forgive him his sins.
So may it be. Amen. 99.
